research: [angle] Michigan QB Bryce Underwood was pulled at halftime vs Penn State after five INTs in his last ten quarters; freshman Tommy Carr (7 career passes) makes his first career start. He went 5-of-7 for 47 yards and ran 36 yards with the go-ahead TD in relief (Predictem, Covers previews, Oct 22-23 2026). Cuts both ways: a less mistake-prone game manager, but a raw passer vs a top-10 defense. Slightly helps Indiana.
Michigan's defense allows the fewest yards per play in the country and about 16 points per game; its run defense allows 2.7 yards per carry (Covers, Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Michigan +7.5.

Michigan's offense ranks outside the top 100 in efficiency per play, per pass and success rate and has not scored more than 21 points in five of six games (Predictem; Covers Top 25 column, Oct 2026). Helps Indiana.
Indiana QB Josh Hoover has 18 TD passes and 0 INTs; Indiana's passing efficiency ranks 15th; Indiana has won or tied the turnover battle in 31 straight games (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Indiana.
Indiana's run game was held to 65 yards vs Nebraska and 73 vs Ohio State, so it may have to throw against the country's stingiest per-play defense (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Michigan.
[angle] Indiana is coming off a 19-15 loss to Ohio State, its first regular-season loss since November 2024, but has won seven straight road games (Predictem, Oct 2026). Neutral to slight Indiana.
Spread: Indiana 1-6 ATS this season, with its last three games decided by 6, 3 and 4 points (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Michigan (priced, tiebreaker only).

Spread/market: line Indiana -7 to -7.5 all week, total 41.5-44.5; no meaningful line move found (Predictem -7, Covers -7.5; Dimers alt -9.5 at +120 is an alternate, not a move). Slate -7.5 at -102 matches the market.
Spread: Michigan has gone under in six of its last seven home games; total 41.5 (Covers, Oct 2026). A low total makes a 7.5 margin relatively large. Mild help to Michigan (priced).

Splits: no public betting percentages found. Expert split: Covers' Marchio and the Covers model took Michigan +7.5; Predictem and SportsGambler took Indiana; Dimers' model projected Indiana 25-18 (about 7).
[angle] Kyle Whittingham's first season at Michigan; the Wolverines lost to Iowa on a last-second drive and to Minnesota before the Penn State win (Predictem, Oct 2026). Neutral.
Weather: about 58F and clear at noon in Ann Arbor (Covers, Oct 2026). Neutral.
games.reasoning: Indiana by about a touchdown matches the line almost exactly: an elite Michigan defense and Indiana's string of one-score games point to Michigan, while Carr's first start against a top defense points to Indiana. The most interesting angle is that Underwood's benching may reduce Michigan's turnovers even as it limits the passing game. No line move and no split data, so it's a pass; a move to Indiana -9 or news on Hoover would have changed it.

research: Northwestern allows about 17 points per game (near the top nationally in scoring defense) and scores 33 (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Northwestern.
Rutgers allows 37 points per game, 125th nationally; Covers' Top 25 column noted its poor available-yards-percentage defense (Predictem, Covers, Oct 2026). Helps Northwestern.
[angle] Northwestern QB Aidan Chiles: 70% completions, 1,398 yards, 9 TD, 0 INT, 7 rushing TDs under new OC Chip Kelly (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Northwestern.

Rutgers QB Dylan Lonergan threw for 291 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT last week but has 5 INTs across Rutgers' three losses (Predictem, Oct 2026). Rutgers can score (26 ppg) but turnovers in catch-up mode. Mixed.

[angle] Northwestern only beat 2-5 Michigan State 24-21 last week after blowing out Penn State 34-13 and Ball State 45-14 (SportsGambler, Covers, Oct 2026). Helps Rutgers (Northwestern not consistently margin-heavy).
Rutgers is off a 37-30 win at Maryland; lost 47-15 at Indiana on Oct 4 (SportsGambler, Oct 2026). Mixed.

Spread/market: Northwestern -14.5 on Oct 22 (SportsGambler), -15.5 at Action Network, -16.5 by game day (Dimers, Covers). About a 2-point move toward the favorite; slate -16.5 is the settled number. Neutral (no edge vs market).
Spread: Rutgers has covered 6 of its last 11; Northwestern has gone over its team total in its last 7 home games (Covers trends, Oct 2026). Mixed, priced.
Spread: Northwestern 5 straight wins at Ryan Field, 8-2 in last 10 home games averaging 27.0-18.8 (SportsGambler, Oct 2026). A 8-point average home margin is short of 16.5. Helps Rutgers slightly.
Model/expert views: Dimers model Northwestern 36-21 with Rutgers 50.6% to cover; Covers Top 25 column took Northwestern -16.5; SportsGambler's correct score 35-14 (Oct 2026). Balanced.
No injury news found for either team in pre-game previews; total 58-58.5.
games.reasoning: Northwestern's defense against a 125th-ranked Rutgers defense justifies a big number, and the market already moved it from 14.5 to 16.5, so the slate line is fair. Rutgers can score with Lonergan, which keeps a backdoor open, but nothing unpriced points either way. Pass; a late Chiles injury or a move back to 14.5 would have changed it.

research: Iowa averages 6.09 yards per carry (3rd nationally) and allows 2.51 (5th), with 3.17 sacks per game (6th) and 14.5 points allowed per game (Predictem, Oct 22 2026). Helps Iowa.
Minnesota averages 3.66 yards per carry (117th); its pass defense ranks 9th and it is 11-for-11 on field goals (Predictem, Oct 22 2026). Mixed.

[angle] Minnesota center Ashton Beers is out for the year, guard Jaden Ball missed the last two games, and Minnesota has used three different starting offensive lines in five games, facing a top-6 sack defense (Predictem, Oct 22 2026). Helps Iowa.

Rest: both previews mention a bye (Minnesota off a bye per Predictem; Iowa's QB numbers 'before the bye' per Covers). Neutral.
Minnesota lost 41-13 to Purdue, allowing 195 rushing yards to one back (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Iowa.
Spread: Minnesota 3-1 ATS at home (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Minnesota (priced).

Spread/market: Iowa -6.5 at Predictem and Covers (Oct 22), -7.5 at one Covers listing, then -4.5 by game day (Dimers -4.5 at -135, later -156; slate -4.5 at -141). A 2-3 point move toward the home underdog, partly offset in the juice. Helps Minnesota (move toward the dog).
[angle] Floyd of Rosedale: Iowa has won 10 of the last 11 meetings and five straight in Minneapolis; last year's meeting was 41-3 (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Iowa (head-to-head, priced).
Expert views: Predictem Iowa -6.5 (24-13); Covers column Iowa -6.5 but Covers' Marchio took Minnesota +6.5; SBR AI Iowa 27-13; Dimers model about Iowa 25-17. No betting splits found. Total 40.5-42.5.
games.reasoning: Locked as a pass because the result leaked before any lean was written down. Before the leak the evidence was split: Iowa's run game and pass rush against Minnesota's patched-up line favored Iowa, while a 2-3 point move toward the home underdog favored Minnesota. The forced side was not formed before the leak; see the contamination note.
games.contaminationNote: A WebSearch summary (allowed_domains included pickswise.com and dimers.com) said a Pickswise matchup page was 'marked final with a score that appears to read Iowa 10, Minnesota 13'. I saw this before writing any lean. Per LESSONS.md I locked a pass. The forced side (Minnesota) rests on the pre-leak line move toward the underdog, but I had not settled it before the leak and it matches the leaked result, so discount it.

UCLA's offense scored 17 points in each of its last two games (17-7 over Wisconsin, a win at Oregon) and ranks 125th in seconds per snap (Covers, WagerTalk, Oct 2026). A slow, defense-led favorite. Helps Michigan State.
UCLA's defense ranks 2nd in EPA per play allowed and 3rd in opponent success rate (36.2%), 11th in havoc, with 19 takeaways, 2nd-most nationally (Covers, WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Helps UCLA.
Michigan State's offense ranks 119th in EPA per play and 133rd in explosiveness; it scored 3, 10 and 13 points against Wisconsin, Notre Dame and Nebraska (Covers, Oct 2026). Helps UCLA.
[angle] Michigan State RB Cam Edwards is out for the season (knee, Sept 26); the Spartans have averaged 3.3 yards per carry since (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Helps UCLA.

[angle] Michigan State is 2-5 straight up but its losses include one point to Illinois and three to Northwestern (24-21 last week); it travels about 2,000 miles (Covers, Oct 2026). Mixed: close-loss team, long trip.
Spread: UCLA 6-0 straight up and 5-0-1 or 6-0 ATS; Michigan State 5-2 ATS (WagerTalk, Covers, Oct 2026). Covers' JD Yonke calls UCLA a 'sell high' spot. Priced; tiebreaker only.

Spread/market: opened UCLA -13.5, moved to -14.5 (briefly -15.5) through the key number 14, with about 88% of spread money on UCLA; total fell from 46.5 to 42.5-43.5 with 'every tracked dollar' on the under (WagerTalk/GoldSheet, Oct 22 2026). Move helps UCLA; slate +15 is half a point better than the -14.5 consensus.

Spread: total 42.5 implies roughly UCLA 28.5-13.5; with UCLA's offense at 17 points the last two weeks, a 15-point margin needs a defensive/turnover-driven blowout (Covers lines, Oct 2026). Helps Michigan State.
Expert views: GoldSheet UCLA -14.5 (28-10), Predictem 24-13, Covers column UCLA -14.5; Covers' Yonke Michigan State +14.5 'at +14 or better'. Weather ideal at the Rose Bowl.
Michigan State has gone under in its last four road games (Covers, Oct 2026). Supports a low-scoring game, which favors the points.
games.reasoning: UCLA's case is almost entirely its defense, with a backup QB and an offense that scored 17 in each of the last two games: the CFB lesson says not to lay big points with a defense-only favorite, and a 42.5 total makes 15 a lot. I project UCLA by about 11.5 (unshaded edge 3.5, shaded ~2), so it's a lean on the underdog. The money on UCLA through 14 gives me pause; if that move were clearly sharp, or if UCLA had its starting QB, this would be a pass.

research: USC's offense is top 10 in success rate (51.6%), leads the nation in first downs and moves the chains on 52% of plays; Jayden Maiava has 2,045 yards, 18 TD, 3 INT; Lincoln Riley called the team its healthiest of the year after the bye (Covers column; Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps USC.

Wisconsin's offense ranks 95th in success rate and its run game 115th; QB Colton Joseph went 6-of-16 for 66 yards at UCLA, and Wisconsin ran 49 plays to UCLA's 71 (Covers; Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps USC.
Wisconsin's defense allows 16.7 points per game and 4.32 yards per play (9th nationally), 287 yards per game (17th) (Predictem; WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Helps Wisconsin +3.
USC's defense allows nearly 6 yards per play and about 239 passing yards per game; Oregon scored 41 on it Sept 26 (Predictem; WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Helps Wisconsin.

[angle] Wisconsin RB Abu Sama III (6.6 yards per carry) is back from missing time; Wisconsin center Austin Kawecki broke his hand, forcing a line reshuffle in which the new right guard has allowed a team-high 13 pressures; UCLA blitzed 76% of dropbacks against them (WagerTalk; Predictem, Oct 2026). Mixed.
[angle] Forecast wind gusts near 30 mph at a 7:30 PM ET kickoff in Madison, USC's first game at Camp Randall since 1965 (Predictem, Oct 2026). Slightly helps the run-heavy home dog / the under.
Spread: USC 2-5 ATS this season; its cover at Penn State was its first Big Ten road cover outside LA County since joining in 2024 (Predictem; WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Helps Wisconsin (priced).

Spread/market: opened USC -2.5; opening-day money and tickets were all on Wisconsin yet the line moved to USC -3; now 67% of money on USC with 53% of tickets on Wisconsin (WagerTalk/GoldSheet, Oct 2026). Suggests bigger/sharper bets on USC. Helps USC.
Spread: total 49.5-50.5 with 82% of total money on the under (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). A low-scoring game keeps a 3-point line live for the dog. Mild help to Wisconsin.
Expert views split: Covers column USC -1.5/-2.5, Predictem USC -3 (27-20); GoldSheet Wisconsin +3 (24-20); Covers AI Wisconsin +2.5. SportsGambler USC 58% to win.
games.reasoning: USC's offense against Wisconsin's anemic attack supports USC, but Wisconsin's top-10 per-play defense, wind and a night home game make a field goal margin the likely shape, which is exactly the line. Money moved it from -2.5 to -3 against the tickets, but the lessons say movement toward a favorite hasn't held. Pass; a hook (USC -2.5) or a firm Kawecki/Sama update would have changed it.
